problem.text: Alice, Bob, and Charlie were on a hike and were wondering how far away the nearest town was. When Alice said, “We are at least $6$ miles away,” Bob replied, “We are at most $5$ miles away.” Charlie then remarked, “Actually the nearest town is at most $4$ miles away.” It turned out that none of the three statements was true. Let $d$ be the distance in miles to the nearest town. Which of the following intervals is the set of all possible values of $d$?

steps.title: Where to start: turn each false statement into its opposite
steps.body: The key phrase is "none of the three statements was true". So each statement is false, which means its opposite is true. Write each statement as an inequality in $d$, then flip it.

your_turn.prompt: Alice said $d \ge 6$. What inequality is true, given that she was wrong?
your_turn.answer: $d < 6$. The opposite of "at least $6$" is "less than $6$".

steps.title: Flip Bob's and Charlie's statements
steps.body: Bob said $d \le 5$, so in fact $d > 5$. Charlie said $d \le 4$, so in fact $d > 4$. Careful with the endpoints: the opposite of "at most" is a strict "more than", so the boundary numbers themselves are not allowed.

your_turn.prompt: Could $d$ be exactly $5$? Explain using Bob's statement.
your_turn.answer: No. If $d = 5$, then "at most $5$ miles" is true, but Bob's statement was false.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: All three facts hold at once, so $d$ must satisfy $d < 6$, $d > 5$ and $d > 4$. Any $d > 5$ is automatically greater than $4$, so the overlap is $5 < d < 6$. Be sure to use all three statements: dropping Alice's leaves $(5,\infty)$, and dropping Bob's leaves $(4,6)$. The answer is **(D)** $(5,6)$.

wrong_choices.E: This comes from ignoring Alice's statement. Since she was wrong about "at least $6$", we also know $d < 6$, which cuts the interval off at $6$.
wrong_choices.C: This comes from ignoring Bob's statement. Since he was wrong about "at most $5$", we also know $d > 5$, which raises the lower end from $4$ to $5$.
